Second, regarding specific characteristics:
whether directed toward oneself or others,
both praise and disparagement are necessarily sinful.
If one were to disparage or praise [the Buddha], would that also be merit?
There are four propositions regarding this.
Some praise demerit and disparage merit; this is because,
respectively, they cause harm to others and bring them benefit.
There are those who praise merit while disparaging it, or disparage sin while praising it;
this is because they seek to destroy heterodoxy and the like,
or because they use flattery to draw in profit.
There are cases where both praise and disparagement constitute merit as well as demerit;
the same applies to disparagement and praise.
This refers, for instance, to that which accords with what is shallow and minor versus that which contradicts what is profound and vast.
There may be cases where praise or blame, or blame or praise, constitutes neither sin nor merit;
this refers, for example, to transgressions or disturbances arising from the predominance of that mind,
or when one is oppressed by severe suffering.
Or, if one who has not yet received the precepts performs an indeterminate act—
such as praising or disparaging a transgression—
it will necessarily constitute a defeat (pārājika).
If one establishes the grounds for defeat (*pārājika*),
would one also praise or disparage?
That is to say, it is difficult to determine with certainty the characteristics of lightness and heaviness.

As stated in the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra-viniścaya-saṃgrahaṇī* and its verses,
I here set forth my own intention,
following the single-fascicle judgment of the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi*.

Fortunately, we share the same aspiration. Examine this thoroughly and reach a definitive conclusion. The subtle and essential mysteries of the sacred scriptures have now been revealed; like a perfect mirror suspended in space, they illuminate the vast heavens. A human birth and the holy teachings are difficult to encounter again; those with the will to escape [saṃsāra] should act while there is still time.
